correctness.rationale: The vertex set is exactly the cross pairs and B-pairs. To see the clipped-hypersimplex equality, aggregate the A-coordinates to a single coordinate in [0,1]; the projection is the second hypersimplex on b+1 coordinates. Decompose into its pair vertices and distribute each cross-pair mass among the A sites in the proportions x_i/x(A), if x(A)>0. The two within-part contrast spaces are spanned by vertex differences and a cross minus a B-pair adds a between-part direction, giving full intrinsic dimension. In the proposed vertex design, covariance along a zero-sum A contrast is p/a times its squared norm; along a zero-sum B contrast the unordered-pair contribution uses sum_{i<j}(z_i+z_j)^2=(b-2)sum_i z_i^2, giving the stated sigma_B with the singleton contribution. The between-block scores differ by sqrt(kappa), giving sigma_T; the cross covariances vanish from block symmetry and conditional mean zero. All eigenvalues are positive including b=2. The determinant has the stated strictly log-concave scalar factor with vanishing endpoints. Multiplication of its stationary equation by positive denominators gives the stated quadratic, and b=2 or 3 gives the stated fractions. Subtracting the two orbit gauges gives (a-1)/p+(1-2p)/(p(1-p))+(3-b)/(b sigma_B), exactly the log-determinant derivative. Their weighted average is d, so at the optimum each is d. Strict convexity excludes all nonvertex contact. For any competitor (m,R) average the containment inequality over the design: 1>=tr(R^{-1}C)+(c-m)^T R^{-1}(c-m). Trace–determinant AM–GM proves det R>=d^d det C with equality only for m=c and R=dC, establishing global uniqueness and the intrinsic volume/semiaxes. The a=2,b=3 example checks directly with p=2/3 and sigma_T=5/27. The 70-digit checker and its recorded 361 scalar and 49 matrix scopes were inspected, not independently run; those finite tests are not the proof.
